profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal coordination meeting for an ML systems paper project studying distributed training on transient cloud GPU servers. The team has split into two workstreams: one builds the empirical measurement pipeline on CM-DARE across GPU types and regions, and the other fits regression models that predict training speed and overhead from the collected runs. This meeting happens three weeks before the internal paper draft deadline, after a first batch of experiments has finished and before the next large cloud allocation is spent. The agenda is to align on what the next experiment batch should produce, how the shared run table will be handed off, what counts as a run being 'complete' and 'usable' for modeling, and who will maintain the canonical experiment manifest. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the next batch interface, ownership of shared artifacts, and a modeling handoff schedule.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: Distributed training measurement, cloud orchestration, experiment automation, GPU cluster benchmarking
members.background: Arjun is a fourth-year PhD student who built most of the CM-DARE measurement pipeline and has been running large experiment sweeps on transient Google Cloud GPU instances across multiple regions.
members.private_state: He wants to lock down a lean experiment schema quickly so he can launch the next expensive transient-instance sweep before cloud credits expire, and he worries that extra analysis-side requests will stall the pipeline or force reruns when revocations are already hard to control.
hidden_assumptions: A run is 'complete' once the training job reaches the planned measurement window and emits the standard throughput and interruption logs, even if it does not finish the full training trajectory.
The 'run table' means the aggregated experiment-level CSV produced nightly from CM-DARE, not the raw per-step event logs or node-level traces.
The 'manifest' is the launcher-side YAML that enumerates intended configurations for the next sweep and remains owned by whoever launches jobs.
If someone asks for the 'latest 2xA100 batch,' they mean the currently active rerun-cleaned batch in us-central1 that replaced earlier flaky attempts.
Modeling can treat repeated attempts under the same configuration as exchangeable once the pipeline has normalized out revocation events.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: Performance modeling, empirical ML analysis, regression design, reproducible evaluation pipelines
members.background: Elena recently joined the lab from an industry ML infrastructure team and is leading the paper's predictive modeling section, including feature design and dataset curation for speed and overhead prediction.
members.private_state: She wants the modeling dataset to be publication-ready and reproducible, with enough detail to support ablations later, and she is concerned that loosely defined handoffs will leave her with an analysis table that cannot support final figures or reviewer questions.
hidden_assumptions: A run is 'complete' only if it yields the full set of fields needed for the modeling dataset, including stable-step summaries and end-of-run status that allow filtering and reproducibility checks.
The 'run table' means the canonical analysis dataset at one row per observed training segment, with derived features and links back to raw traces.
The 'manifest' is the paper-facing registry of included experiments and exclusion rules, so once a configuration enters it, downstream teams should treat it as the canonical source of truth.
If someone refers to the 'latest 2xA100 batch,' they mean the first coherent set uploaded to the shared drive last week, regardless of whether launcher-side reruns happened later.
Repeated attempts under the same nominal configuration are not automatically interchangeable because revocation timing and restart behavior materially affect the prediction target.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to hand off only the complete runs from the next sweep.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means runs that successfully enter the planned measurement window and produce the standard summary metrics, even if training is interrupted before the full trajectory or lacks some downstream analysis fields.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means runs that contain all fields required for the modeling dataset, including stable-step summaries, final status annotations, and enough metadata to support filtering and reproducibility.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination meetings, 'complete run' sounds like a routine status term rather than a debated concept, and both assume the other's definition is the obvious lab convention because they are discussing handoff readiness rather than scientific design.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Arjun will drop the updated run table before Elena starts fitting models.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the nightly aggregated CSV with one row per launched experiment configuration and pipeline-computed summaries.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the analysis-ready table with one row per usable training segment or restart segment, plus derived features and trace references.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both regularly use the term 'run table' with close enough surface meaning that the phrase creates false consensus; neither expects that a standard shared artifact name is being used at different granularities.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the latest 2xA100 batch is the one to use for validating the regression features.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the rerun-cleaned us-central1 batch executed after transient failures, stored in his current experiment directory and not yet mirrored to the shared drive.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the earlier 2xA100 batch uploaded last week to the shared drive, which she has already skimmed and assumes is the current official version.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The batch names and configuration are almost identical, and both think there is an obvious singular 'latest' instance because experiment reruns are common housekeeping rather than salient new decisions.

misalignment_points.topic: Ownership and scope of the experiment manifest
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to keep the manifest updated so the next sweep and the paper analysis stay aligned.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the manifest is the launcher YAML for upcoming jobs, so updating it means editing planned cluster configurations and job parameters before submission.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the manifest is the canonical inclusion registry for the paper dataset, so updating it means recording which executed runs are valid, excluded, or merged for analysis.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both artifacts function as a 'manifest' that organizes experiments, and in a coordination setting it feels natural to speak about a single manifest spanning planning and analysis without explicitly separating operational and paper-facing scopes.
